proof:
# Exact failure of the dependence-component rank budget

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): counterexample proved. For a finite lattice-convex set P in Z^k with dependence components P_i, the proposed inequality

    sum_i 2^(dim aff P_i) <= 2^k

is false already at k=3. The rank-cost allocation route is therefore blocked. This does not contradict the proved Helly additivity inequality `sum_i h(P_i)<=2^k`, and is not an OC counterexample.

## 1. A five-vertex polytope with nine integer points

Set

    a=(0,0,1), b=(0,0,3), d=(0,2,1),
    f=(1,2,0), h=(2,0,0),
    Q=conv{a,b,d,f,h},   P=Q intersect Z^3.

The complete integer list is

    a=(0,0,1), e=(0,0,2), b=(0,0,3),
    j=(0,1,1), t=(0,1,2), d=(0,2,1),
    v=(1,0,1), f=(1,2,0), h=(2,0,0).                 (1)

Here is a direct finite certificate of the list. Every point of Q lies in the integer bounding box

    0<=x<=2, 0<=y<=2, 0<=z<=3

and satisfies the six supporting inequalities

    2x+y+4z>=4,    x+z>=1,    x>=0,    y>=0,
    x+y+z<=3,      6x+3y+4z<=12.                      (2)

Checking the 36 integer box points against (2) gives exactly (1). Conversely all listed points belong to Q: besides the five defining vertices,

    e=(a+b)/2,    j=(a+d)/2,    t=(b+d)/2,
    v=a/4+b/4+h/2.                                  (3)

Thus this certificate proves the exact integer set without assuming that the displayed inequalities have no additional noninteger vertices. In particular P is lattice-convex by construction.

The five defining points are all exposed vertices. For example a uniquely minimizes x+y+z, b uniquely maximizes z, d uniquely maximizes 2y-x, f uniquely maximizes x+2y, and h uniquely maximizes x. All comparisons are among the five defining vertices and are strict.

## 2. Exact dependence components

The minimal faces of the four nonvertices in (1) are

    e: edge [a,b],
    j: edge [a,d],
    t: edge [b,d],
    v: triangle conv{a,b,h}.                          (4)

For e, use the supporting planes x=y=0. For j, use x=0 and x+z=1. For t, use x=0 and x+y+z=3. For v, use y=0 and the strictly positive three coefficients in (3). These supporting faces are exactly the indicated edge or triangle, as is seen directly from the five vertices.

The hyperedges generated by (4) connect every listed point except f. Explicitly the three populated edges join a,b,d,e,j,t, and the populated triangle joins h and v to a,b. Thus

    P_1=P minus {f},    P_2={f}.                      (5)

There is no hidden representation connecting f to this component. The point f is an exposed vertex and cannot be the target of a nontrivial anchored representation. Every other possible nonvertex target is one of e,j,t,v and lies on x=0 or y=0. Since f has x>0 and y>0 while both coordinates are nonnegative throughout Q, it cannot occur with positive coefficient in a representation of any such target. The other four vertices also admit no nontrivial anchored representations.

The determinant of the three columns b-a, d-a, h-a is -8. Hence P_1 has full affine rank three, whereas P_2 has rank zero. Therefore

    2^(dim aff P_1)+2^(dim aff P_2)=8+1=9>8=2^3.       (6)

## 3. Helly values, verified by a complete exact finite certificate

The actual finite-set Helly numbers are

    h(P_1)=5,    h(P_2)=1,    h(P)=6.                 (7)

The attached Fraction verifier checks these values exhaustively. To make the finite computation a mathematical certificate, the criterion is as follows. For any finite S, its Helly number is the largest size of a nonempty W subset S for which

    S intersect intersection_(w in W) conv(W minus {w}) is empty. (8)

Indeed a minimal infeasible convex family C_1,...,C_N has distinct witnesses w_i in S belonging to every C_j with j!=i. Then conv(W minus {w_i}) lies in C_i, proving (8). Conversely the convex sets in (8) form an infeasible family, and deletion of its w-indexed member leaves w in all remaining members.

For each subset of the nine-point set, the verifier computes its exact convex closure using Caratheodory's theorem in R^3: membership is tested on all affinely independent subsets of at most four points by rational Gaussian elimination and nonnegative barycentric coordinates. It then tests (8) for every W. The lower-bound witnesses it finds are

    W_1={a,e,j,t,v} for P_1,
    W={a,e,j,t,v,f} for P.

Thus the rank-budget failure is consistent with exact Helly additivity: 5+1=6<=8. The rank cost 8 of the large component overcharges its actual Helly cost 5.

## 4. Counterexamples in every larger integer dimension

For k=3+q, take Q times [0,1]^q. Its integer set is P times {0,1}^q. A convex representation whose last q coordinates are a cube vertex can use only sources with those same coordinates. Therefore its dependence components are separate copies of P_1 and P_2 at every cube vertex. Their rank cost is

    2^q(8+1)=9*2^(k-3)>2^k.

The k=3 certificate alone refutes the proposed universal inequality; this product shows that the failure persists in all k>=3. No claim about a complete low-dimensional classification is needed or inferred.
